fixes.find: It often decides the comparison. R-22 is no longer produced. Equipment still running it depends on reclaimed supply, and a single large leak can end the repair path on its own. New equipment now ships with A2L refrigerants, which carry different line sizing, leak detection and handling rules than the R-410A generation. Reusing an existing line set is a question of condition and compatibility, not a given, and a contaminated circuit should not be carried into new equipment. City & Suburban repairs all makes and models, so a building can stage replacement while older equipment stays serviceable.
fixes.replace: It often decides the comparison. R-22 is no longer produced. Equipment still running it depends on reclaimed supply. A single large leak can end the repair path on its own. Much new equipment now uses A2L refrigerants, but not all of it does. Where an A2L unit is chosen, line sizing, leak detection and handling rules can differ from the R-410A generation. Which rules apply depends on the equipment category, the refrigerant selected, the current transition rules and the maker's instructions. Reusing an existing line set is a question of condition and compatibility, not a given. A contaminated circuit should not be carried into new equipment.
fixes.why: MAJOR faq: qualify blanket A2L claim by equipment category, refrigerant, transition rules and manufacturer; shorter sentences (READ-02)

fixes.find: Phased replacement can keep unaffected business spaces operating while another area closes, provided the systems can be separated. Before ordering equipment, identify the first area affected and the condition for returning it to service. Record business hours, access restrictions and temperature-sensitive activities when preparing for the shutdown. No fixed outage duration fits every building. A tenant should coordinate landlord approval and the building access contact before announcing a closure. After the exchange, operating instructions should explain how occupied spaces return to normal use.
fixes.replace: Before ordering, the replacement scope should confirm curb or pad fit and electrical and gas capacity. It should say whether any retained coil or air handler is compatible with the new equipment. It should name the refrigerant, the rules that apply to it, and who removes and disposes of the old unit. Phased replacement can keep unaffected spaces open while another area closes, if the systems can be separated. Identify the first area affected and when it returns to service. No fixed outage duration fits every building. A tenant should get landlord approval and an access contact before announcing a closure.
fixes.why: MAJOR install: replace generic intro with the replacement decision (curb fit, gas/electrical capacity, retained coil compatibility, refrigerant rules, shutdown planning, disposal)
